lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable:
## Statement

For every positive integer $d$, the integer lattice $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ is at most countable. Countability here means finite or in bijection with $\mathbb{N}$, as in [[def-countable]].
def-qsm-local-spin-algebras:
## Definition

Fix an integer dimension $d\ge1$, the countable site set $\Gamma=\mathbb{Z}^d$ of [[lem-qsm-integer-lattice-countable]], and one finite spin dimension $q\ge1$. Equip $\Gamma$ with the max-coordinate metric $d_\infty(x,y)=\max_{1\le r\le d}|x_r-y_r|$; symmetry and separation hold coordinatewise, and the triangle inequality follows from $|x_r-z_r|\le|x_r-y_r|+|y_r-z_r|$ for every coordinate. A **finite region** is a finite subset $\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma$; its cardinality is $|\Lambda|$.

For a finite region $\Lambda$, let $S_\Lambda=\{1,\ldots,q\}^{\Lambda}$ be the set of spin configurations on $\Lambda$ and let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be the vector space of functions $f:S_\Lambda\to\mathbb C$ with inner product $\langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}f(s)\overline{g(s)}$. For each $s\in S_\Lambda$, let $e_s$ be the indicator function of $\{s\}$; these vectors form an orthonormal basis. For $\Lambda=\varnothing$, $S_\Lambda$ is a singleton and $\mathcal H_\Lambda\cong\mathbb C$. The **local spin matrix algebra** is

$$\mathcal A_\Lambda:=\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)\cong M_{q^{|\Lambda|}}(\mathbb C),$$

Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\Lambda)$ denotes all complex-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional Hilbert space; they are bounded. The algebra has composition, Hilbert adjoint, identity $I_\Lambda$, and induced operator norm

$$\|T\|:=\sup_{\|\xi\|=1}\|T\xi\|.$$

The **finite local trace** is $\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(T):=\sum_{s\in S_\Lambda}\langle T e_s,e_s\rangle$ in the displayed configuration basis $(e_s)$. This is the usual finite-matrix trace; basis independence and its cyclic/unitary identities are supplied by [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]].

If $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, restriction of configurations gives the canonical factorization $\mathcal H_{\Lambda'}\cong\mathcal H_\Lambda\otimes\mathcal H_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$, with sites ordered lexicographically. The **factor inclusion** is the unital $*$-homomorphism $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}:\mathcal A_\Lambda\to\mathcal A_{\Lambda'}$ given by $T\mapsto T\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. A **localization region** for $T$ is any finite $\Lambda$ for which $T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ under these inclusions; a localization region need not be minimal.

The ordinary operator norm makes each local matrix algebra a nonzero unital complete C*-algebra, and every positive normalized complex-linear functional is uniquely a trace pairing with a density matrix, by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]]. This includes the empty region, whose Hilbert space is $\mathbb C$. This definition does not posit an infinite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert space.
lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric:
## Statement

Fix $d\ge1$, $q\ge1$, and finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Then the factor inclusion $\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)=T\otimes I$ is an isometric unital $*$-homomorphism:

$$\|\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}(T)\|=\|T\|\qquad(T\in\mathcal A_\Lambda).$$

For nested finite regions $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'\subseteq\Lambda''$, the inclusions compose: $\iota_{\Lambda',\Lambda''}\circ\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda'}=\iota_{\Lambda,\Lambda''}$.
def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra:
## Definition

Use the finite local matrix algebras and isometric factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]] and [[lem-qsm-local-spin-inclusions-isometric]]. Identify $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ with its image in every larger finite-region algebra. The directed union

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}:=\bigcup_{\Lambda\subseteq\Gamma,\ |\Lambda|<\infty}\mathcal A_\Lambda$$

is the algebra of **strictly local observables**. Its norm is $\|A\|=\|A\|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ for any finite localization region $\Lambda$ of $A$; isometric inclusions make this independent of the chosen region. The **quasi-local spin algebra** is the norm completion

$$\mathcal A:=\overline{\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}}^{\,\|\cdot\|}.$$

The C*-algebra structure on this completion has product and adjoint extended continuously from the finite local matrix algebras. Countable Choice is assumed for the published existence theorem for metric completions; [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]] supplies the full extension argument using the finite C*-identity of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]].

**No global Hilbert tensor product is selected.** “Quasi-local” means norm completion of the directed algebra of finite-region observables; it does not mean a chosen representation as operators on an infinite tensor-product Hilbert space. A local operator $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ may have more than one localization region. Disjoint finite local factors commute in their common finite tensor algebra.
lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the Cauchy-sequence completion. For the local spin system of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], the normed $*$-algebra $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and its completion $\mathcal A$ of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]] are well defined; $\mathcal A$ is a unital complex C*-algebra and $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is norm dense in it. If $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$ and $B\in\mathcal A_\Delta$ for disjoint finite regions $\Lambda,\Delta$, then $AB=BA$.
def-qsm-infinite-algebraic-state:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal A$ be the unital quasi-local spin C*-algebra of [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]], whose C*-structure uses Countable Choice as in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]]. An **infinite algebraic state** is a bounded complex-linear functional $\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathbb C$ satisfying $\omega(I)=1$ and $\omega(A^*A)\ge0$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$.

For each finite region $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$, the restriction $\omega|_{\mathcal A_\Lambda}$ is a finite-matrix state. By [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], every positive normalized functional on a finite matrix algebra is represented by a unique density matrix. Define its **local density matrix** $\rho_\Lambda$ by

$$\omega(A)=\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)\qquad(A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda),$$

where $\rho_\Lambda=\rho_\Lambda^*\ge0$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}\rho_\Lambda=1$. For $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$, the local densities are **consistent** when $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$, with partial trace characterized by its pairing against every $A\otimes I_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}$. No density operator on a globally chosen Hilbert space is part of this definition.

This agrees with the canonical state convention of [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]: the finite restrictions have norm one by [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]], giving $|\omega(A)|\le\|A\|$ on the dense local algebra and hence on its completion; evaluation at the norm-one identity gives $\|\omega\|=1$. Conversely a canonical state has local restrictions with density matrices of trace one, since the finite norm formula and continuity on the dense local algebra imply $\|\omega\|=\omega(I)$. No global density representation is asserted.
lem-qsm-consistent-local-states:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice for the norm completion in [[def-qsm-quasilocal-spin-algebra]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be positive trace-one matrices, one on each finite-region algebra $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]], such that for every $\Lambda\subseteq\Lambda'$ their partial traces agree: $\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda'\setminus\Lambda}(\rho_{\Lambda'})=\rho_\Lambda$. There is a unique infinite algebraic state $\omega$ on $\mathcal A$ whose restriction to each $\mathcal A_\Lambda$ is $A\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}_{\Lambda}(\rho_\Lambda A)$.
lem-qsm-spin-state-compactness:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the countable union of finite regions and the finite-dimensional state/density interface explicitly stated in Facts [F3]. Let $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$, and $q\ge1$ be as in [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. For every sequence of algebraic states $\omega_n$ on the quasi-local spin algebra $\mathcal A$, there is a subsequence $\omega_{n_k}$ and an algebraic state $\omega$ such that $\omega_{n_k}(A)\to\omega(A)$ for every $A\in\mathcal A$. Thus the state space is sequentially compact in the pointwise topology, meaning convergence on every fixed observable. The conclusion concerns functional values; it does not assert convergence of global density matrices or a global trace-class representation.
lem-qsm-state-gns-construction:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the C*-algebra completion interface of [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]], and the finite-matrix positive square-root interface of [[lem-qsm-matrix-state-calculus]]. Let $\{\rho_\Lambda\}$ be a consistent family of finite local density matrices as in [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], and let $\omega$ be its extended algebraic state on the unital quasi-local algebra $\mathcal A$. Then there are a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H_\omega$, a unital $*$-representation $\pi_\omega:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\omega)$, and a unit vector $\Omega_\omega$ cyclic for $\pi_\omega$ such that

$$\omega(A)=\langle \pi_\omega(A)\Omega_\omega,\Omega_\omega\rangle\qquad(A\in\mathcal A),$$

using the linear-first inner-product convention. Here $\mathcal B(\mathcal H_\omega)$ is the space of bounded linear operators with its operator norm, a $*$-representation is a complex-linear map preserving products, adjoints and the identity, and cyclic means that $\{\pi_\omega(A)\Omega_\omega:A\in\mathcal A\}$ is norm dense in $\mathcal H_\omega$. The theorem asserts existence of a cyclic representation, not uniqueness up to unitary equivalence.
ex-qsm-quasilocal-two-site-locality:
## Statement

Take $d=1$, spin dimension $q=2$, and distinct sites $x,y\in\mathbb Z$. On $\mathbb C^2$ define the Pauli matrices

$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

Let $X_x$ and $Z_y$ be their one-site observables embedded in the two-site algebra $\mathcal A_{\{x,y\}}$ by the factor inclusions of [[def-qsm-local-spin-algebras]]. Then $X_x$ and $Z_y$ are self-adjoint unitaries of norm one and commute. This is a finite example of the locality clause in [[lem-qsm-quasilocal-completion]].
ex-qsm-quasilocal-infinite-tail-observab:
## Statement

Take $d=1$ and $q=2$. For $n\ge1$, let $Z_n$ be the one-site Pauli matrix $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$ embedded at site $n\in\mathbb Z$. The sequence

$$H_N:=\sum_{n=1}^N2^{-n}Z_n$$

converges in norm in the quasi-local algebra to an element $H$. This element is self-adjoint but has no finite localization region. Thus norm completion adds observables that are not strictly local.
ex-qsm-maximally-mixed-consistent-produc:
## Statement

Fix finite spin dimension $q\ge1$ on $\Gamma=\mathbb Z^d$, $d\ge1$. For every finite region $\Lambda$, set

$$\rho_\Lambda:=q^{-|\Lambda|}I_\Lambda.$$

This is a consistent family of maximally mixed local density matrices. By the finite-dimensional density-state correspondence of [[lem-qsm-finite-matrix-cstar-and-state-duality]] and [[lem-qsm-consistent-local-states]], it determines a unique algebraic state $\omega$ on the quasi-local spin algebra. For local $A\in\mathcal A_\Lambda$, its expectation is $\omega(A)=q^{-|\Lambda|}\operatorname{Tr}_\Lambda(A)$.
